title: Cred gatekeeper shim and signalable async-iterables; unify retry telemetry and parity bump
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
Motivation: Customers reported confusing semantics when credentials rotated during long-lived streaming consumers and inconsistent telemetry across SDKs for retry events. This PR introduces a lightweight 'credential gatekeeper' that centralizes lookups and prevents mid-stream token races, and a signalable async-iterable wrapper that lets consumers observe lifecycle events (reauth, pause, resume) for improved ergonomics. Additionally, retry telemetry events (backoff start/stop, final attempt) were normalized across Python/TS/Go SDKs to make server-side correlation simpler.

What this changes (high level): central credential gatekeeper library (py/ts/go) that manages in-flight token handoffs; signalable async-iterable abstraction for streaming responses (exposes on_signal hooks: REAUTH_REQUESTED, CONNECTION_PAUSE, CONNECTION_RESUME, ERROR_RETRY); normalized retry telemetry labels and envelope fields across SDKs; small TS/Go parity fixes around token refresh time parsing and default jitter window. No changes to server API.

Implementation notes: the gatekeeper exposes a minimal API: acquire_credential(context_id) and register_listener(context_id, callback) - implementations are adapter-idiomatic per language, intentionally tiny to preserve embeddability in SDKs. The async-iterable wrapper decorates existing stream consumers and emits well-documented signals; it is opt-in (consumers opt into signalable_stream). Retry telemetry uses a compact envelope (retry_phase, attempt_number, backoff_ms, final) that we now emit from client-side retry hooks and include in telemetry metadata.

Checklist:
- [x] Python implementation (redwood-sdk-python): gatekeeper module, wrapper for AsyncGenerator-based streams, unit tests
- [x] TypeScript implementation (redwood-sdk-typescript): gatekeeper, async-iterator decorator, integration tests in examples
- [x] Go implementation (redwood-sdk-go): cred adapter, context-aware iterator helper, tests
- [x] Telemetry events emitted from retry middleware across all three SDKs
- [x] Docs updated in each SDK package README with examples and migration notes
- [x] Version bumps: py 1.45.0 -> 1.46.0, ts 1.27.3 -> 1.28.0, go v1.8.9 -> v1.9.0

Testing: unit tests cover gatekeeper concurrency (token swap under 100 concurrent acquires), signalable stream lifecycle with simulated token expiry mid-stream, and telemetry emission count/labels. Integration smoke runs with the local devserver using short-lived test credentials. CI initially failed on TypeScript lint (missing semicolon in examples) and on a flaky Go test around context cancel handling; both were fixed in follow-up commits.

Backward compatibility: All changes are opt-in defaults. Existing consumers that do not opt into 'signalable_stream' or 'gatekeeper' will see no behavior changes. Token acquisition semantics are preserved except for improved ordering guarantees under heavy contention.

Related: references ENG-3245 (user-reported stream auth races), ENG-3301 (observable retry telemetry), SUP-71234 (customer incident follow-up).

review_comments: Dmitri Volkov (review): The gatekeeper looks clean; please ensure we don't introduce an additional goroutine per acquire in Go - prefer a shared worker pattern.
Priya Nambiar (reply): Updated Go impl to use a shared waiter map and condition variable; removed per-acquire goroutine (see commit 4).
Leah Morgan (review): Can we reduce telemetry cardinality by avoiding full token ids in payloads? Also add example showing how to hook on REAUTH_REQUESTED.
Priya Nambiar (reply): Agreed — telemetry now uses token_family hash (stable low-cardinality) and example demonstrates REAUTH_REQUESTED handler.
Owen Park (approval): Verified python unit tests and manual smoke run. Approving pending TS lint fix.

merge_outcome: merged via squash (squash and merge) by Priya Nambiar after approvals. Changelog entries added to each SDK's CHANGELOG.md and release PRs scheduled.
release_notes: Introduce optional credential gatekeeper and signalable_stream helpers across Python/TS/Go SDKS. Normalizes retry telemetry envelope for server-side correlation. Opt-in ergonomics improvements; no breaking changes by default. Version bumps: python 1.46.0, typescript 1.28.0, go v1.9.0.
notes_for_operators: Operators: telemetry now exposes retry_phase and attempt_number; update any alerting rules that relied on previous free-form retry messages. No server config changes required. If you run private deployments with custom SDKs, coordinate upgrades to avoid mixed-client telemetry schemas.
migration_steps: 1) Consumers who want observable stream lifecycle should enable signalable_stream in the client options and register on_signal callbacks. 2) If you previously parsed token expiry strings in TS/Go, prefer SDK helper parse_token_expiry that tolerates millis and seconds. 3) For downstream telemetry pipelines, start reading retry_envelope fields instead of ad-hoc retry log lines.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps gatekeeper API minimal to reduce surface area for future refactors. Follow-ups planned: add a small server-side guidance doc and example for stateful token families and TTL tuning.
